introduction to physics.definition: Physics is the branch of science that studies matter, energy and the interaction between them.

measurement ii.definition: Measurement II deals with accurate measurements using precision instruments such as the Vernier calipers and the micrometer screw gauge.

vernier_calipers.purpose: Measures internal diameter, external diameter, thickness and depth.

micrometer_screw_gauge.purpose: Measures very small diameters and thicknesses.

zero_error.definition: A reading shown by an instrument when the correct reading should be zero.

formulae: Actual Reading = Main Scale Reading + Vernier Reading
Correct Reading = Observed Reading − Positive Zero Error
Correct Reading = Observed Reading + Negative Zero Error
key_points: Always check for zero error before taking measurements.
Read the scale at eye level to avoid parallax error.
Use the ratchet on the micrometer to avoid over-tightening.

worked_examples.question: Main scale = 2.30 cm, Vernier reading = 0.06 cm. Find the reading.
Observed reading = 5.62 mm, Positive zero error = 0.02 mm.

practice_questions: State the least count of a Vernier calipers.
State the least count of a micrometer screw gauge.
How do you avoid parallax error?
answers: A reading shown when the instrument should read zero.
Read the scale directly at eye level.

force.definition: A force is a push or pull acting on an object that can change its state of rest or motion.
key_points: A force has magnitude and direction.

worked_examples.question: A body of mass 5 kg accelerates at 4 m/s². Find the force.
Find the weight of a 12 kg object if g = 10 m/s².

practice_questions: Calculate the force acting on a 6 kg object accelerating at 2 m/s².
answers: A force is a push or pull acting on a body.
Starts motion, stops motion, changes speed and changes direction.
Mass is the amount of matter in a body while weight is the gravitational force acting on the body.

practice_questions: List the seven SI base units.
answers: Physics is the study of matter and energy.
Mechanics, Optics, Thermodynamics and Electricity.
Medicine, Engineering, Agriculture, Communication and Transport.
metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela.

measurement i.definition: Measurement is the process of comparing a physical quantity with an accepted standard unit.
key_points: Use the correct instrument for the quantity being measured.

worked_examples.question: Convert 5 km to metres.
Convert 300 cm to metres.

answers: Measurement is comparing a quantity with a standard unit.
Metre, kilogram, second and kelvin.
Metre rule, tape measure, vernier calipers and micrometer screw gauge.
Looking at the scale from the wrong angle.

pressure.definition: Pressure is the force acting normally per unit area.
key_points: Pressure acts at right angles to a surface.
applications: Sharp knives have small surface areas.

facts: Pressure depends on the density of the liquid.

atmospheric_pressure.definition: Atmospheric pressure is the pressure exerted by the weight of air.

hydraulic_machines.principle: Pressure applied to a confined liquid is transmitted equally in all directions (Pascal's Principle).

worked_examples.question: A force of 120 N acts on an area of 4 m². Calculate the pressure.
Pressure is 200 Pa over an area of 5 m². Find the force.

practice_questions: State the SI unit of pressure.
Why do tractors have wide tyres?
answers: Pressure is force acting normally per unit area.
Pascal (Pa).
To reduce pressure on the ground.
Pressure applied to a confined liquid is transmitted equally in all directions.
Hydraulic jack and hydraulic brakes.

particulate nature of matter.definition: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space. Matter is made up of tiny particles called molecules or atoms.
kinetic_theory: Matter is made of tiny particles.

diffusion.definition: Diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration.
examples: Perfume smell spreading in a room.

brownian_motion.definition: Brownian motion is the random movement of tiny particles suspended in a fluid.

worked_examples.question: Why does the smell of perfume spread across a room?
worked_examples.solution: Because perfume particles diffuse through the air from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration.

worked_examples.question: Why do gases fill the whole container?
worked_examples.solution: Gas particles move freely in all directions and occupy all available space.

practice_questions: State the three states of matter.
State four assumptions of the kinetic theory of matter.
answers: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.
Solid, liquid and gas.
Diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration.
Brownian motion is the random movement of tiny particles suspended in a fluid.
Matter is made of particles; particles are always moving; particles have spaces between them; heating increases particle movement.

thermal expansion.definition: Thermal expansion is the increase in the size of a substance when heated and the decrease in size when cooled.
applications: Overhead electric cables are left slack.
advantages: Helps fit metal rims on wooden wheels.

worked_examples.question: Why are gaps left between railway tracks?
worked_examples.solution: To allow the rails to expand when heated and prevent buckling.

worked_examples.question: Why are electric wires installed loosely?
worked_examples.solution: They contract in cold weather and expand in hot weather.

practice_questions: State the three types of expansion.
Give four applications of thermal expansion.
State two disadvantages of thermal expansion.
answers: Thermal expansion is the increase in size of a substance when heated.
Linear, area and volume expansion.
Railway lines, bridges, thermometers and thermostats.
Buckling of railway lines and cracking of bridges.

heat transfer.definition: Heat transfer is the movement of heat energy from a hotter body to a colder body.

conduction.definition: Transfer of heat through a substance without movement of the substance.
examples: Heating one end of a metal rod.

convection.definition: Transfer of heat by movement of liquids or gases.

radiation.definition: Transfer of heat by electromagnetic waves without the need for a material medium.

applications: Cooking utensils are made of metals.
Saucepan handles are made of wood or plastic.

worked_examples.question: Why are cooking pots made of aluminium?
worked_examples.solution: Because aluminium is a good conductor of heat.

worked_examples.question: Why are saucepan handles made of plastic?
worked_examples.solution: Because plastic is a poor conductor of heat.

practice_questions: State the three methods of heat transfer.
Why does a vacuum flask reduce heat loss?
answers: Heat transfer is the movement of heat from a hotter body to a colder body.
Conduction, convection and radiation.
Heating a metal rod and cooking with a metal saucepan.
Cool air from the sea moves to replace warm rising air over land.
It reduces heat transfer by conduction, convection and radiation.

temperature and thermometers.definition: Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.

difference_between_heat_and_temperature.heat: Heat is a form of energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder body.
difference_between_heat_and_temperature.temperature: Temperature is the measure of the hotness or coldness of a body.

thermometers.maximum_minimum: Measures the highest and lowest temperatures.

worked_examples.question: Convert 27°C to Kelvin.
Convert 310 K to Celsius.

practice_questions: State four properties of a good thermometric liquid.
answers: Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
Heat is energy while temperature measures hotness.
Uniform expansion, visible, does not wet glass and responds quickly.

linear motion.definition: Linear motion is motion along a straight line.

distance.definition: Distance is the total length of the path travelled.

displacement.definition: Displacement is the shortest distance from the starting point to the ending point in a specified direction.

speed.definition: Speed is the distance travelled per unit time.

velocity.definition: Velocity is displacement per unit time in a given direction.

acceleration.definition: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.

key_points: Acceleration may be positive or negative.

worked_examples.question: A car travels 240 m in 20 s. Calculate its speed.
A body changes velocity from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 5 s. Find its acceleration.

practice_questions: State the SI unit of acceleration.
Calculate the speed of a cyclist travelling 150 m in 30 s.
Calculate the acceleration of a body whose velocity changes from 8 m/s to 20 m/s in 4 s.
answers: Distance is the total length of the path travelled.
Speed is scalar while velocity has direction.
m/s².
5 m/s.
3 m/s².

reflection of light.definition: Reflection is the bouncing back of light when it strikes a surface.
laws_of_reflection: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
The incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.

terms.incident_ray: The ray that strikes the surface.
terms.reflected_ray: The ray that leaves the surface after reflection.
terms.normal: A line drawn at 90° to the reflecting surface.
terms.angle_of_incidence: The angle between the incident ray and the normal.
terms.angle_of_reflection: The angle between the reflected ray and the normal.

types_of_reflection.regular: Occurs on smooth polished surfaces producing clear images.
types_of_reflection.diffuse: Occurs on rough surfaces producing unclear images.

properties: Image is the same size as the object.

formulae: Angle of Incidence = Angle of Reflection

worked_examples.question: If the angle of incidence is 35°, find the angle of reflection.
An object is placed 50 cm in front of a plane mirror. Find the image distance.

practice_questions: State the two laws of reflection.
Differentiate between regular and diffuse reflection.
State five characteristics of images formed by a plane mirror.
An incident ray strikes a mirror at 60°. Find the angle of reflection.
answers: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection; incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.
Reflection is the bouncing back of light from a surface.
Regular reflection occurs on smooth surfaces while diffuse reflection occurs on rough surfaces.
Virtual, upright, same size, laterally inverted and equal image distance.

electrostatics.definition: Electrostatics is the study of electric charges at rest.

charges.positive: Produced when an object loses electrons.
charges.negative: Produced when an object gains electrons.

electroscope.definition: An electroscope is an instrument used to detect the presence and type of electric charge.

worked_examples.question: What happens when a positively charged rod is brought near a negatively charged object?
worked_examples.solution: They attract each other because unlike charges attract.

worked_examples.question: State one method of charging a body.

practice_questions: State the law of electric charges.
What is the function of an electroscope?
answers: Electrostatics is the study of electric charges at rest.
Like charges repel while unlike charges attract.
Friction, contact and induction.
To detect electric charge.
Photocopiers and electrostatic spray painting.

cells and simple circuits.definition: An electric cell is a source of electrical energy that converts chemical energy into electrical energy.

series.description: Components are connected in one path.
disadvantages: If one component fails, the whole circuit stops working.

parallel.description: Components are connected on separate branches.

key_points: Current flows only in a closed circuit.
A switch opens or closes a circuit.
Electric current is measured in amperes (A).

worked_examples.question: A circuit has a voltage of 12 V and a resistance of 4 Ω. Calculate the current.
Why does a bulb go off when the switch is opened?
worked_examples.solution: Because opening the switch breaks the circuit and stops current flow.

practice_questions: Differentiate between primary and secondary cells.
State three components of a simple circuit.
Differentiate between series and parallel circuits.
Calculate the current if V = 9 V and R = 3 Ω.
answers: An electric cell converts chemical energy into electrical energy.
Primary cells cannot be recharged while secondary cells can.
Cell, switch and bulb.
Series has one path while parallel has several branches.
